title: System Engineer Intern
description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Job Description As a High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Product & System Engineering Intern, you will contribute to the validation and optimization of Micron’s HBM products —the fastest and highest-capacity HBM available. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers to develop innovative solutions for testing and integrating HBM into customer platforms, helping advance generative AI and high-performance computing. Responsibilities Develop and improve software and hardware to validate HBM in various systems. Configure, maintain, and characterize HBM-based systems in a lab environment. Assist in debugging complex technical challenges across hardware and software. Communicate results and insights to teammates and leadership. Learn and apply knowledge of HBM, DRAM, and memory systems. Minimum Qualifications Enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program or equivalent experience in Electrical or Computer Engineering. Graduation date must be after September 2027. Strong understanding of computer architecture, memory systems, and memory technologies. Proficiency in Python, C/C++, and scripting for debugging and testing. Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills. Enthusiastic teammate with strong communication skills and a proactive approach. Preferred Qualifications Validate hardware, firmware, and software products through testing, debugging, and cross-functional integration. Use Linux environments and RTL modeling techniques with Verilog/SystemVerilog for design validation and development. Program, debug, and troubleshoot FPGAs and microcontrollers in lab and prototyping environments. Apply knowledge of memory interfaces and protocols including LPDDR, DDR, HBM, GDDR, CXL, UCIe, and PCIe. Utilize lab equipment such as oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, while communicating complex technical concepts effectively through written and verbal presentations. As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future. title: AI Compiler and Kernel Intern – Summer 2027
description: NVIDIA is looking for an AI Compiler & Kernel Intern to apply AI agents, machine learning, and performance engineering to compilers, GPU kernels, and developer tools. You will work with compiler, kernel, and AI engineers on a scoped project involving code, compiler and kernel feedback, performance experiments, and optimization. Depending on your background and interests, the work may focus on agentic workflows, learned models, compiler optimization, GPU kernel development, performance analysis, or AI-enabled developer tools. Candidates may enter from either a compiler or kernel background; experience in every area is not expected. What You’ll Be Doing: Build AI-agent workflows that interact with code, compilers, GPU kernels, benchmarks, performance tools, and engineering systems. Develop tools that help agents collect data, run experiments, analyze compiler, kernel, and performance feedback, identify optimization opportunities, and recommend next steps. Explore data-driven approaches for compiler optimization, GPU kernel generation and tuning, performance prediction, decision support, and workflow automation. Build reliable interfaces between AI agents and compiler, kernel, or developer-tool infrastructure. Prototype improvements to compiler flows, code generation, GPU kernels, optimization tools, experimentation systems, or developer workflows. Work with compiler, kernel, architecture, AI, and performance engineers to evaluate ideas on representative workloads. Measure correctness, runtime performance, compile time, resource utilization, reliability, and other relevant outcomes. Document the design, experiments, results, limitations, and next steps. What We Need to See: Pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a similar field . Strong programming skills in Python, C, C++, or a similar language. Solid foundations in data structures, algorithms, software engineering, and quantitative problem solving. Coursework, research, or project experience in one or more of these areas: AI, machine learning, AI agents, compilers, programming languages, GPU kernels, CUDA or accelerator programming, systems, performance engineering, optimization, or developer tools. Ability to design experiments, analyze results, investigate technical problems, and communicate findings clearly. Experience working in one or more of AI, compiler, kernel, performance, or systems areas, with the ability to learn across technical boundaries. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Experience building AI agents, LLM applications, evaluation systems, coding workflows, or developer tools. Experience with LLVM, MLIR, compiler optimization passes, code generation, domain-specific languages, or compiler infrastructure. Experience writing, analyzing, or optimizing GPU kernels using CUDA, Triton, or a similar accelerator programming model. Hands-on experience with reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, predictive modeling, ranking, search, or high-dimensional data analysis. Research, internships, open-source contributions, or personal projects that measure runtime, compile time, resource use, code quality, or developer productivity Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 20 USD – 94 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 6, 2026. title: Research Scientist Intern - PAR Safety Evals and Red Teaming
description: Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. In the pursuit of personal superintelligence, Meta's AI systems are becoming more capable, and evaluating their safety is critical. Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Safety Evals and Red Teaming team within the Products and Applied Research org. We are seeking individuals passionate in areas such as Agent Safety, Benchmarks and Evaluations, Synthetic Data Generation, Automated Red teaming, LLM-as-a-Judge, benchmark design, eval harnesses, prompt injection, agent environments. Our internships are 16 weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year. What You Could Work On: Depending on your interests and the team’s priorities, a project could address questions such as: • How reliably do LLM-based judges identify safety-policy violations across different tasks, prompts, and adversarial conditions? How should we measure their errors and consistency? • How should we evaluate prompt-injection risks when an agent interacts with tools and untrusted information? Which environments and attack scenarios expose failures that simpler tests miss? • Which automated red teaming methods uncover meaningful safety failures, and how well do those failures generalize beyond the prompts or environments used to find them? • How can we use synthetic data and benchmark design to improve coverage while checking that scores reflect the behavior we intend to measure?

title: Math Libraries Intern
location: Canada; Santa Clara, CA; United States
description: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world. NVIDIA is looking for software engineering interns to join the math libraries team building cuEST , a CUDA-X math library that accelerates quantum chemistry on NVIDIA GPUs. Launched in March 2026, cuEST provides accelerated APIs for essential functions in electronic structure computations, starting with Gaussian-basis quantum chemistry. These capabilities power applications ranging from drug discovery to semiconductor process development. We are constantly working to improve the feature set, performance, and technology stack of cuEST. If the idea of helping expand the frontiers of electronic structure theory excites you, come join our team and help us build GPU-accelerated software used by quantum chemists around the world. During your internship, you will work with senior engineers on the cuEST team who will mentor you and guide you in developing highly optimized algorithms and numerical methods for quantum chemistry. Projects may involve implementing new quantum chemistry primitives, defining APIs, analyzing and improving GPU performance, finding solutions for difficult numerical corner cases, and other software engineering work that goes into shipping a production CUDA-X library. What you’ll be doing: Prototype and develop GPU-accelerated algorithms for Gaussian-basis quantum chemistry primitives in cuEST. Analyze the performance of CUDA implementations, identify opportunities for improvement, and implement them. Contribute across the engineering lifecycle, from design and testing to code that ships in the library. Collaborate with team members and other stakeholders to understand how quantum chemistry applications use cuEST and what they need from it. What we need to see: Pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD degree in Computational Chemistry, Computational Physics, Computer Science, Applied Math, or an equivalent program area. Excellent C/C++ or Python programming, debugging, performance analysis, and test design skills. Strong algorithms and numerical methods fundamentals. Ability to work independently and lead your own development effort. Good teamwork, communication, and documentation habits. Ways to stand out from the crowd: GPU programming experience (CUDA or OpenCL) is desired but not required. Coursework or research experience in quantum chemistry or electronic structure theory is desired but not required. Knowledge of floating-point arithmetic and numerical error analysis. Knowledge of CPU or GPU hardware architecture. Experience using agentic AI tools to improve the speed and quality of software development. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you’re creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you! Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 20 USD – 94 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 6, 2026.
